likeNew.label: Like New
likeNew.fullDescription: Opened but essentially untouched. This game looks like you just removed the shrink wrap. Many games get opened, admired, and put on the shelf - if that's your game, this is probably the right grade.
boxCriteria: No visible wear, scuffs, or scratches
No shelf wear or storage marks
componentCriteria: All components present and accounted for
Cards show no wear - edges crisp, no bowing
Tokens unpunched, or punched with no damage
likeNew.proTip: If you've played even once or twice, consider Very Good instead. Like New means essentially untouched.

veryGood.label: Very Good
veryGood.fullDescription: Played and enjoyed, but handled with care. A game in Very Good condition is what you'd happily give as a gift.
boxCriteria: Minor shelf wear or light scuffing
No tears, splits, or structural damage
componentCriteria: Cards show minimal handling - light edge wear at most
Tokens punched cleanly, no lifting or tearing
veryGood.proTip: This is the sweet spot for most second-hand games. Buyers get a great game at a fair price.

good.label: Good
good.fullDescription: Clearly pre-loved - this game has seen regular play but remains fully functional. All the adventures, some of the wear.
boxCriteria: Corner wear - soft corners, possible minor splits
Light ring wear or sticker residue
componentCriteria: All components present (or missing pieces clearly noted)
Cards show shuffling wear on edges
Boards may have minor warping or edge wear
good.proTip: Many collectors are happy with Good condition for games they want to play rather than display.

acceptable.label: Acceptable
acceptable.fullDescription: Well-loved and showing it. This game works, but it's seen better days. Always note what's missing or damaged in your listing description - buyers deserve to know exactly what they're getting.
boxCriteria: Corner splits, tears, or tape repairs
componentCriteria: All crucial components present (minor pieces may be missing)
Cards worn - may need sleeves to play comfortably
Boards may have noticeable wear or warping
acceptable.proTip: Be very specific about damage. 'Acceptable with taped corner' is better than vague descriptions.

punchedTokens.title: Punched vs unpunched tokens
punchedTokens.description: Whether cardboard tokens have been punched from their sheets matters to some buyers.
details: Unpunched: tokens still in their original sheets
Cleanly punched: removed carefully with no damage

sleevedCards.title: Sleeved cards
sleevedCards.description: Cards protected in sleeves are a plus. Note this in your listing.

paintedMinis.title: Painted miniatures
paintedMinis.description: Some buyers want painted minis, others don't. Be clear about the state.

philosophy.title: When you're unsure
philosophy.content: If you're debating between two grades, go with the lower one. A buyer who receives a game in better condition than expected is delighted.

page.title: Help Centre
page.description: Guides and resources for buying and selling pre-loved board games on Second Turn Games.

q1.question: What is Second Turn Games?
q1.answer: Second Turn Games is a peer-to-peer marketplace for buying and selling pre-loved board games in the Baltic region (Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia). Every listing is verified against BoardGameGeek's database of 170,000+ games.

q2.question: Where can I sell board games in Latvia?
q2.answer: Second Turn Games is the dedicated marketplace for selling board games in Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia. List your games with verified BoardGameGeek data, set your price, and ship via parcel lockers. Sellers receive 90% of the sale price.

q3.question: Is Second Turn Games safe?
q3.answer: Yes. Second Turn Games uses EveryPay (via Swedbank) for secure payment processing, offers buyer protection with a dispute resolution window, and verifies all listings against BoardGameGeek's database. The platform is operated by Second Turn Games SIA, registered in Latvia.

q4.question: What are the fees on Second Turn Games?
q4.answer: Buyers pay the item price plus a flat €2.00 shipping fee (no service fee). Sellers pay a 10% commission on the item price, deducted automatically. Listing is free.

q5.question: How does selling on Second Turn Games work?
q5.answer: Search for your game in the BoardGameGeek database, grade its condition, set a price, add photos, and publish. When someone buys, you confirm the order within 24 hours, pack the game, and drop it off at a parcel terminal. Your earnings are credited to your wallet after delivery.

q6.question: How does shipping work on Second Turn Games?
q6.answer: Second Turn Games uses Unisend parcel terminals across the Baltic region. Shipping costs a flat €2.00 per order. After confirming an order, sellers receive a shipping code, pack the game, and drop it off at any Unisend terminal. Tracking updates automatically.

q7.question: How do I get paid as a seller?
q7.answer: Two days after delivery (or when the buyer confirms earlier), your earnings (90% of item price) are credited to your platform wallet. You can withdraw to your IBAN bank account at any time - no fees, no minimum waiting period.

q8.question: What board game conditions are accepted?
q8.answer: Second Turn Games uses four condition grades: Like New (played 1-2 times, all components present), Very Good (light wear, fully playable), Good (moderate wear, complete and playable), and Acceptable (noticeable wear but complete). All grades require complete, playable games.
